findings.title: Negative offset is passed straight to queryset slicing and raises ValueError
findings.body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, when enable_advanced_features is set and cursor.offset < 0, start_offset is set to the raw negative offset and then used as queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django does not support negative indexing on querysets and raises ValueError, so the request fails with a 500. The client controls this value: a cursor string such as '1:-5:0' parses to a negative offset via Cursor.from_string. The comment that says this is 'safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level' is incorrect; permissions have nothing to do with slicing. The same applies to the base BasePaginator.get_result path for is_prev cursors (line 182 in the base path passes a negative offset through when is_prev is set).

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates BasePaginator.get_result nearly verbatim
findings.body: The new class copies most of BasePaginator.get_result (cursor handling, hits counting, prev-row trimming, build_cursor call) and adds only a negative-offset branch that is broken (see the line 882 finding). Any future fix to the base logic will silently diverge in this copy. The class also duplicates get_item_key and value_from_cursor, which are already identical to DateTimePaginator's behavior for the sort keys used here. The change should either extend BasePaginator with a flag or be reverted.

findings.title: Experimental pagination path is gated by a client query parameter and an admin-only flag
findings.body: The optimized paginator is selected by the client-supplied query parameter optimized_pagination=true, and it enables advanced features for superusers and users with global access. This ships an unreviewed, experimental code path (negative offset handling that the code comments describe as allowing 'access to data beyond normal pagination bounds') to production behind a user-controlled switch. The comment claiming permissions are enforced at the queryset level is not backed by any check in the code. Access checks should be explicit and tested, or the path should not be exposed.

findings.title: Deploy will break in-flight segments stored as Redis sets
findings.body: process_spans now uses ZADD on span-buf:s:* keys, and add-buffer.lua switched from SCARD/SUNIONSTORE to ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE. Any span-buf:s:* key written by the previous code is a Redis set, so ZADD, ZCARD and ZUNIONSTORE on it fail with WRONGTYPE, and _load_segment_data's ZSCAN fails as well. Segments buffered before the deploy (up to span_buffer_timeout / root timeout, and the queue entries still reference them) will error during processing and flushing. No key migration, dual-read, or key renaming is included.

findings.title: Span eviction silently discards data with no log or metric
findings.body: When a segment exceeds 1000 spans, zpopmin removes the lowest-scored (oldest) spans from the set. Those spans are dropped without any counter, log, or metric. The previous Python-side guard (max_segment_spans) did emit metrics and an error log, and that check has now been removed from _load_segment_data. Operators have no way to see that segments are being truncated.

findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE sums scores for duplicate payloads
findings.body: ZUNIONSTORE uses the default SUM aggregate. When the same span payload is present in both the source and destination sets (for example, a redelivered Kafka message), its score is doubled, so its end_timestamp_precise no longer reflects the span's real end time. This distorts the eviction order introduced by this PR (zpopmin evicts by score) and any ordering that depends on it. An explicit AGGREGATE MIN or MAX should be used, or duplicates should be otherwise handled.

findings.title: Redirect loop limit reduced from 10000 to 1000 without updating dependent behavior
findings.body: The redirect-walk loop bound was lowered from 10000 to 1000 and the explanatory comment about deep segment trees was removed. Trees with a redirect depth above 1000 will now be silently left unjoined, where previously they were joined. This is a behavior change that is not mentioned in the PR and has no test covering depth above 1000.

findings.title: max_segment_spans is now a dead parameter
findings.body: The max_segment_spans check was removed from _load_segment_data, but SpansBuffer.__init__ still accepts and stores max_segment_spans (default 1001). Nothing reads it, so the configuration is misleading: callers believe they can tune a span-count limit that no longer does anything. The Lua limit of 1000 is now the only span cap and is hardcoded.

findings.title: Hard KeyError on messages lacking end_timestamp_precise
findings.body: process_batch now reads val["end_timestamp_precise"] directly. Any span message without that field (for example from an older Relay or a schema gap) raises KeyError and fails the whole batch in the consumer, rather than being handled or defaulted. The rest of the code already uses .get() for optional fields such as parent_span_id and is_remote.

findings.title: No tests for the new eviction, the 1000-span cap, or the optimized paginator
findings.body: The PR adds spans-per-segment eviction via zpopmin and a new OptimizedCursorPaginator with negative-offset handling, but no tests cover either. There is no test that inserts more than 1000 spans and checks which survive, no test for duplicate payload score aggregation, and no test for negative or is_prev cursor offsets in pagination. The existing negative-offset bug would have been caught by a single test.
